claim: Black Basta uses Windows Command Shell.
description: Black Basta is ransomware written in C++ that has been offered within the ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) model since at least April 2022; there are variants that target Windows and VMWare ESXi servers. Black Basta operations have included the double extortion technique where in addition to demanding ransom for decrypting the files of targeted organizations the cyber actors also threaten to post sensitive information to a leak site if the ransom is not paid. Black Basta affiliates have targeted multiple high-value organizations, with the largest number of victims based in the U.S. Based on similarities in TTPs, leak sites, payment sites, and negotiation tactics, security researchers assess the Black Basta RaaS operators could include current or former members of the Conti group.

ref-1c01244a9abeecd66b33.text: DarkGate uses a malicious Windows Batch script to run the Windows code utility to retrieve follow-on script payloads. DarkGate has also used `cmd.exe` to create a remote shell. DarkGate has stolen `sitemanager.xml` and `recentservers.xml` from `%APPDATA%\FileZilla\` if present. DarkGate has used WMI to execute files over the network and to obtain information about the domain. DarkGate has deleted all files in the Mozilla directory using the following command: `/c del /q /f /s C:\Users\User\AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\firefox*`. DarkGate has deleted its staging directories. DarkGate attempts to steal Opera cookies, if present, after terminating the related process. DarkGate has used the `shutdown`command to shut down and/or restart the victim system. DarkGate has used PowerShell to create a remote shell.
ref-1c01244a9abeecd66b33.title: McGraw, T. (2024, December 4). Black Basta Ransomware Campaign Drops Zbot, DarkGate, and Custom Malware. Retrieved December 9, 2024.

ref-27769a411a26b4494c2c.text: OSX/Shlayer can escalate privileges to root by asking the user for credentials. OSX/Shlayer can masquerade as a Flash Player update. OSX/Shlayer can base64-decode and AES-decrypt downloaded payloads. Versions of OSX/Shlayer pass encrypted and password-protected code to openssl and then write the payload to the /tmp folder. If running with elevated privileges, OSX/Shlayer has used the spctl command to disable Gatekeeper protection for a downloaded file. OSX/Shlayer can also leverage system links pointing to bash scripts in the downloaded DMG file to bypass Gatekeeper, a flaw patched in macOS 11.3 and later versions. OSX/Shlayer has been Notarized by Apple, resulting in successful passing of additional Gatekeeper checks. OSX/Shlayer has executed a .command script from a hidden directory in a mounted DMG. OSX/Shlayer can use the chmod utility to set a file as executable, such as chmod 777 or chmod +x. OSX/Shlayer has relied on users mounting and executing a malicious DMG file. OSX/Shlayer has collected the IOPlatformUUID, session UID, and the OS version using the command sw_vers -productVersion. OSX/Shlayer can use bash scripts to check the macOS version, download payloads, and extract bytes from files. OSX/Shlayer uses the command sh -c tail -c +1381... to extract bytes at an offset from a specified file. OSX/Shlayer uses the curl -fsL "$url" >$tmp_path command to download malicious payloads into a temporary directory. OSX/Shlayer can download payloads, and extract bytes from files. OSX/Shlayer uses the curl -fsL "$url" >$tmp_path command to download malicious payloads into a temporary directory.
ref-27769a411a26b4494c2c.title: Carbon Black Threat Analysis Unit. (2019, February 12). New macOS Malware Variant of Shlayer (OSX) Discovered. Retrieved August 8, 2019.

ref-2e5ce0b63b29a50bf2af.text: Raspberry Robin uses rundll32 execution without any command line parameters to contact command and control infrastructure, such as IP addresses associated with Tor nodes. Raspberry Robin retrieves its second stage payload in a variety of ways such as through msiexec.exe abuse, or running the curl command to download the payload to the victim's %AppData% folder. Raspberry Robin uses newly-registered domains containing only a few characters for command and controll purposes, such as "v0[.]cx". Raspberry Robin uses regsvr32.exe execution without any command line parameters for command and control requests to IP addresses associated with Tor nodes. Raspberry Robin uses mixed-case letters for filenames and commands to evade detection. Raspberry Robin uses msiexec.exe for post-installation communication to command and control infrastructure. Msiexec.exe is executed referencing a remote resource for second-stage payload retrieval and execution. Raspberry Robin uses the Windows utility odbcconf.exe to execute malicious commands, using the regsvr flag to execute DLLs and bypass application control mechanisms that are not monitoring for odbcconf.exe abuse. Raspberry Robin is capable of contacting the TOR network for delivering second-stage payloads. Raspberry Robin has historically been delivered via infected USB drives containing a malicious LNK object masquerading as a legitimate folder. Raspberry Robin uses cmd.exe to read and execute a file stored on an infected USB device as part of initial installation. Raspberry Robin will communicate via HTTP over port 8080 for command and control traffic. Raspberry Robin uses outbound HTTP requests containing victim information for retrieving second stage payloads. Variants of Raspberry Robin can download archive files (such as 7-Zip files) via the victim web browser for second stage execution. Raspberry Robin has historically used infected USB media to spread to new victims. Raspberry Robin will use the legitimate Windows utility fodhelper.exe to run processes at elevated privileges without requiring a User Account Control prompt.
ref-2e5ce0b63b29a50bf2af.title: Lauren Podber and Stef Rand. (2022, May 5). Raspberry Robin gets the worm early. Retrieved May 17, 2024.

ref-5cfc4ffcfb2a23805431.text:
Black Basta has used WMI to execute files over the network.
QakBot can remotely create a temporary service on a target host.
Black Basta has used PowerShell scripts for discovery and to execute files over the network.
ref-5cfc4ffcfb2a23805431.title: Inman, R. and Gurney, P. (2022, June 6). Shining the Light on Black Basta. Retrieved March 8, 2023.

ref-65082134b025312c3931.text:
QakBot has been delivered in ZIP files via HTML smuggling.
QakBot has the ability to use DLL side-loading for execution.
Black Basta will check for the presence of a hard-coded mutex `dsajdhas.0` before executing.
Black Basta can use `cmd.exe` to enable shadow copy deletion.
ref-65082134b025312c3931.title: Vilkomir-Preisman, S. (2022, August 18). Beating Black Basta Ransomware. Retrieved March 8, 2023.

ref-682ef650c2902a5b2e0e.text:
Black Basta can make a random number of calls to the `kernel32.beep` function to hinder log analysis.
The Black Basta dropper has been digitally signed with a certificate issued by Akeo Consulting for legitimate executables used for creating bootable USB drives.
The Black Basta dropper has mimicked an application for creating USB bootable drivers.
Black Basta can use LDAP queries to connect to AD and iterate over connected workstations.
Black Basta can check system flags and libraries, process timing, and API's to detect code emulation or sandboxing.
The Black Basta dropper can check system flags, CPU registers, CPU instructions, process timing, system libraries, and APIs to determine if a debugger is present.
Black Basta can enumerate specific files for encryption.
Black Basta had added data prior to the Portable Executable (PE) header to prevent automatic scanners from identifying the payload.
ref-682ef650c2902a5b2e0e.title: Check Point. (2022, October 20). BLACK BASTA AND THE UNNOTICED DELIVERY. Retrieved March 8, 2023.

ref-70f8a6b23b3622256b99.text:
Black Basta can encrypt files with the ChaCha20 cypher and using a multithreaded process to increase speed. Black Basta has also encrypted files while the victim system is in safe mode, appending `.basta` upon completion.
Black Basta has set the desktop wallpaper on victims' machines to display a ransom note.
ref-70f8a6b23b3622256b99.title: Ballmer, D. (2022, May 6). Black Basta: Rebrand of Conti or Something New?. Retrieved March 7, 2023.

ref-8e620fad0a4725a97166.text:
J-magic can compare the host and remote IPs to check if a received packet is from the infected machine.
J-magic can monitor incoming C2 communications sent over TCP to the compromised host.
J-magic can communicate back to send a challenge to C2 infrastructure over SSL.
The J-magic agent is executed through a command line argument which specifies an interface and listening port.
cd00r can monitor for a single TCP-SYN packet to be sent in series to a configurable set of ports (200, 80, 22, 53 and 3 in the original code) before opening a port for communication.
J-magic can rename itself as “[nfsiod 0]” to masquerade as the local Network File System (NFS) asynchronous I/O server.
cd00r can monitor incoming C2 communications sent over TCP to the compromised host.
J-magic has a pcap listener function that can create an Extended Berkley Packet Filter (eBPF) on designated interfaces and ports.
J-magic can overwrite previously executed command line arguments.
J-magic can monitor TCP traffic for packets containing one of five different predefined parameters and will spawn a reverse shell if one of the parameters and the proper response string to a subsequent challenge is received.
ref-8e620fad0a4725a97166.title: Black Lotus Labs. (2025, January 23). The J-Magic Show: Magic Packets and Where to find them. Retrieved February 17, 2025.

ref-9b574769bb75e0e70e79.text: Black Basta can check whether the service name `FAX` is present.
ref-9b574769bb75e0e70e79.title: Cyble. (2022, May 6). New ransomware variant targeting high-value organizations. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

ref-aa464e2cece70a65b294.text:
Black Basta has been downloaded and executed from malicious Excel files.
Black Basta has used `ShellExecuteA` to shut down and restart the victim system.
ref-aa464e2cece70a65b294.title: Gonzalez, I., Chavez I., et al. (2022, May 9). Examining the Black Basta Ransomware’s Infection Routine. Retrieved March 7, 2023.

ref-c20ca3bdb913e007d8db.text:
QakBot has placed its payload in hidden subdirectories.
QakBot has been packaged in ISO files in order to bypass Mark of the Web (MOTW) security measures.
ref-c20ca3bdb913e007d8db.title: Kenefick, I. et al. (2022, October 12). Black Basta Ransomware Gang Infiltrates Networks via QAKBOT, Brute Ratel, and Cobalt Strike. Retrieved February 6, 2023.

ref-d9106019c38a6cc23c29.text: The Black Basta binary can use `chmod` to gain full permissions to targeted files.
ref-d9106019c38a6cc23c29.title: Sharma, S. and Hegde, N. (2022, June 7). Black basta Ransomware Goes Cross-Platform, Now Targets ESXi Systems. Retrieved March 8, 2023.

ref-f657cbac07dd51c55c88.text:
Black Basta can reboot victim machines in safe mode with networking via `bcdedit /set safeboot network`.
Black Basta can enumerate volumes.
Black Basta has established persistence by creating a new service named `FAX` after deleting the legitimate service by the same name.
Black Basta can delete shadow copies using vssadmin.exe.
Black Basta has the ability to use native APIs for numerous functions including discovery and defense evasion.
Black Basta can collect system boot configuration and CPU information.
Black Basta has modified the Registry to enable itself to run in safe mode, to change the icons and file extensions for encrypted files, and to add the malware path for persistence.
Black Basta can create a new service to establish persistence.
ref-f657cbac07dd51c55c88.title: Zargarov, N. (2022, May 2). New Black Basta Ransomware Hijacks Windows Fax Service. Retrieved March 7, 2023.
